newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: CONFIDENCE IN AVIATION AUTHORITY ERODING

There are growing doubts about the effectiveness of the Civil Aviation Safety Authority. Federal Transport Minister, John Sharp, says public confidence in the authority is eroding, and questions are being asked if its board is adequately doing its job.
Mr Sharp has again written to the Civil Aviation Safety Authority, raising concerns, following the crash of a Barrier Air plane on Sunday near Cairns.
SAFETY REVIEW AFTER STAGECOACH ACCIDENT
The management of Sovereign Hill at Ballarat, in south west Victoria, will review safety procedures at the tourist village after a stagecoach rolled there yesterday.

Police say 18 tourists were aboard the coach when one of five horses bolted, causing the the rollover. Fifteen people were taken to hospital with cuts, bruising and fractures, and some have had surgery.
The director of Sovereign Hill, Peter Hiscock, says the village has just completed an extensive review of safety, but the latest incident will be investigated.
ROW OVER TOPLESS BAR STAFF BILL
The Federal Opposition says bar staff and other hospitality workers could be sacked if they refuse to go topless, under a clause in the Government's industrial relations bill.
The Senate today votes on the clause which if passed, will effectively remove the sexual harrassment section from the hospitality award.
Opposition Industrial Relations spokesman Bob McMullan says employers will no longer be banned from dismissing workers for refusing to dress in a way that causes the employee embarassment.
He says that will do nothing towards protecting the rights and dignity of Australian women.
NSW GETS SECURITY TIPS FROM BRITISH GOVERNMENT
New South Wales Premier Bob Carr has signed a police co-operation agreement with the British Government, aimed at improving security at the Sydney Olympics.
The agreement includes co-operation between the New South Wales and British police forces on the exchange of specialist law enforcement officers, and high-tech security equipment.
Mr Carr says he believes British experience in fighting Irish Republican Army terrorism and international crime will be very useful in the lead up to the 2000 Games.
EUTHANASIA BILL GOES TO SA PARLIAMENT
A voluntary euthanasia Bill will be introduced into the South Australian Parliament today.
Labor MLC, Anne Levy says she'll bring her Bill into the Upper House not just as a token effort, but to seek the full support of Parliament to give hopelessly ill people autonomy and choice.
Ms Levy says the Bill is based on the Northern Territory's legislation.
But it also allows for advance requests for voluntary euthanasia by people who fear illness might prevent them from communicating their wishes.
Ms Levy says a current request would always over-ride an advance request.
WA INTRODUCES NEW NATIVE TITLE LAWS FOR MINING INDUSTRY
The future holders of mining titles in Western Australia will be responsible for Native Title compensation.
The WA Government says the new measure is necessary to clarify who would be responsible for any liability that might come from the granting of a mining title.
Mines minister, Kevin Minson says the mining industry isn't happy with the move, but says the government can't disregard possible liabilities for future taxpayers.
He says the holders of mining titles will be responsible for native title compensation when the titles are granted or worked.
Mr Minson says the State will remain responsible for any compensation from mining titles issued in the past.
CONFERENCE GOES AHEAD DESPITE BAN
Delegates from 25 countries have begun arriving in the Malaysian capital, Kuala Lumpur, for a conference on East Timor....despite the conference being banned by the Malaysian government.
Organisers are defying the ban and say the Asia Pacific Conference on East Timor will go ahead on Friday.
The ban was declared because the Malaysia government says it will create friction between its country and Indonesia.
Nobel Laureate Jose Ramos Horta was intending to address the conference, but he now says he won't be attending because he has no intention of embarrassing Malaysia.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
